LIMITATIONS.md

Verification boundaries and unresolved work

This is a research and engineering atlas. Exact checkpoint/image compatibility still requires runtime validation. It was assembled and audited on October 15, 2026 using publisher cards and configurations, engine recipes, selected source files and pull-request/release metadata. The audit record documents corrections and file coverage.

Completed

Eight model-family directories contain architecture dimensions, technical explanations, precision variants, serving hypotheses, validation plans and source links. The audit resolved exact publisher and derivative revisions, checked immutable metadata, revisited engine releases and main references, and rechecked selected implementation files and relevant PRs. Local code and document checks are reported in VALIDATION. HTTP success alone is not counted as verification of a claim; retrieval receipts and reviewer findings are recorded separately.

The subsequent engine experiment roadmap expands the stable/main/nightly research into proposed investigations. It includes a manual experiment-record template, not a new execution system. Its applicability checks and promotion thresholds must be completed for the actual image, node and workload. Existing profile source references remain their original reviewed snapshots; new research does not silently certify those profiles against a newer nightly.

Not completed or not available

No model weight tensors were downloaded and no inference engine was installed or run. Limited safetensors header metadata was read to check GLM parameter accounting. No B300 node was exercised, and no GPU correctness, throughput, latency, memory or power measurement was performed. No deployed KServe cluster was changed or validated. No nightly container was pulled or tested; source inspection does not certify a nightly binary.

The original assembly failed to clone vLLM and SGLang because that environment could not resolve GitHub; clone-attempt.log preserves that historical result. HTTPS retrieval and the atlas repository's Git fetch succeeded during this audit. Full upstream clones were not repeated. Selected immutable source files were retrieved directly, and clone_upstreams.py remains available for pinned checkouts. Complete upstream repositories are not bundled.

The exact OEM string “B300 SXM6-AC” was supplied by the user and was not independently identified. The hardware discussion uses NVIDIA’s B300 documentation conditionally; CPU, networking, physical topology, cooling, firmware, power limits and usable memory need actual node inventory. A DGX B300 reference specification does not identify the user's server.

Configuration fields are curated projections, not complete original configs. Exact model and variant revisions resolved in the audit are recorded in the model records, profiles and evidence lock. Hypothetical or unidentified variants retain null identities. Immutable links and response hashes improve traceability, but complete raw cards/configs and source trees are not bundled. Mutable recipes and branch heads remain dated observations. Local checksums establish consistency of local files, not historical authenticity or model quality.

Several precision requests have no independently audited exact release: in particular a fully FP8 Kimi K3 is not established. Some derivative repositories are supported by an engine recipe rather than a separately inspected complete export. These distinctions remain visible in the catalog and profiles; missing facts are not filled with neighboring model values.

DeepSeek's family parameter headlines are not an exact July-31 tensor census. GLM's approximately 743B target and 753B full checkpoint are distinguished using the extra MTP layer's header metadata; the accounting is not a GPU memory measurement. Advertised context limits do not establish accuracy or practical concurrency at that length. Licenses in the catalog are identification notes; the applicable base and derivative terms require separate inspection.

Meaning of “best” in this repository

Recommendations are starting hypotheses justified by memory architecture, available implementation paths and source evidence. A winner requires the same workload, input/output distribution, quality threshold, latency target, hardware, effective precision and natural speculative acceptance. Published author benchmarks are not reproduced results. In particular, simulated-acceptance Kimi DSpark results cannot certify application speedup.

The model benchmark guide and expanded family validation plans propose quality suites and matched experiments. Named suites have not been installed or executed, and their endpoint adapters have not been qualified for these checkpoints. The streaming probe does not retain answers for later scoring; an external evaluator must capture and score outputs. Newly identified candidate exports/drafters in a validation plan are not catalogued launch profiles or established runtime support.

VALIDATION.md

Local validation results

Audit, engine-expansion and model-benchmark retrieval date: October 15, 2026 UTC (October 16 in Europe/Paris for the expansion). Supported interpreter used for the recorded local checks: Python 3.12.14.

Actual executions

68 unit tests passed on Python 3.12.14. The documented supported minimum remains Python 3.10. The suite covers memory arithmetic, immutable metadata identity, launch/probe gates, profile topology and context consistency, synthetic-acceptance rejection, redirect handling, exclusive checkout destinations, KServe rendering guards, streaming completion semantics, catalog integrity and offline HTML generation. Network behavior and engine invocations in the tests use mocks.

The repository validator passes for 8 model families, 6 companies and 34 profiles. Model JSON records and individual profile JSON files match their catalog copies. JSON parsing, Python compilation, source IDs and local Markdown links pass. Exact current file/link/source counts are in local-validation.json. The engine expansion and model-benchmark follow-up add documentation and a manual JSON run-record template; they add no execution code or measured serving results. The 68-test suite was rerun for the model-benchmark changes on the interpreter above; no new tests were added.

Seven CLI smoke checks passed: weight arithmetic, ordinary GQA KV arithmetic, guarded dry-run launch, dry-run clone commands, metadata listing without network, benchmark help and KServe renderer help. The illustrative calculations returned 2.8e12 bytes for uniform FP8 at 2.8T parameters and 88 GiB for the stated Mistral KV example. These are calculations, not GPU allocation measurements.

The offline edition is rebuilt from the corrected Markdown. build_atlas.py --check checks freshness; the HTML tests check escaping, internal links, duplicate IDs, formatting and embedded source hashes. SHA256SUMS covers the committed artifacts except the checksum manifest itself.

Primary-source retrieval and review

During the original audit, all eight base model APIs and immutable configurations were independently retrieved by the coordinator, confirming revision, layer count and hidden size. Model reviewers checked the full curated projections and exact derivative metadata. The initial 62 source URLs and all 135 URLs in that audit's integrated register returned HTTP 200 in separate access checks. See the audit report for those independent reviews and corrections. The subsequent engine update records its additional primary-source research and reviews separately. The model benchmark update records fresh model/engine checks, benchmark documentation and selected evaluator-source inspections, plus independent reviews. Accessibility alone does not establish claim accuracy.

Actual Hub and GitHub HTTPS retrieval succeeded. During the engine expansion, GitHub REST requests hit an unauthenticated rate limit; official HTML, raw files and Git references supplied the cited alternatives. Temporary filtered/shallow upstream Git metadata was used where documented for release-versus-main source comparison. The original full-clone failures remain historical evidence; complete upstream clones were not repeated. The metadata downloader's mocked tests are distinct from an end-to-end integration test of that command against the Hub.

Explicitly not tested

No weight tensors were downloaded, no inference engine or serving container was installed or run, and no B300 model-quality, throughput, latency, power or GPU-memory measurement was performed. Only metadata, including limited GLM safetensors headers, was retrieved. No natural speculative acceptance was measured. No container image or nightly wheel was downloaded or tested. No Kubernetes admission check or deployment was performed. KServe unit tests use synthetic image digests to exercise syntax and structure without a registry lookup.

Reproduce

Use Python 3.10 or newer. The recorded audit used:

python3.12 scripts/validate_repo.py
python3.12 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3.12 scripts/build_atlas.py --check

Full unit output is in tests/last-run.txt. Passing local checks does not certify a serving configuration.

benchmarks/MODEL-BENCHMARKS.md

Choose benchmarks for the model and the decision

All runs on this page are proposed. No model-quality or GPU result has been measured in this atlas. Use the engine experiment roadmap to choose the system change and this page to choose the evidence that would justify it. The family validation pages below define the exact model/export prerequisites.

Instructions that needed more detail

Gap in the earlier plansRequired instructionWhy it changes the decision
Lists of precision, context and parallelism settings without a specific quality testSelect a task, scorer and reference before each sweepFaster generation can conceal lost instruction following, retrieval or tool correctness.
One generic quality thresholdPredeclare thresholds by critical task, language, modality and context bucketA mean score can conceal a regression in the workload that matters.
A benchmark name without its evaluation contractPin dataset, split, selected item IDs, scorer, prompt construction, reasoning budget and output extractionTwo runs bearing the same benchmark name can measure different tasks.
Several profile differences attributed to one featureCompare a matched control or label the result as a complete-configuration comparisonKV dtype, EP, autotuning, cache allocation and speculation can change together.
Successful HTTP/SSE completion treated as a useful answerTrack protocol completion, task success and latency compliance separatelyA length-limited or filtered completion can pass transport checks and still fail the task.
Throughput evidence without saved answersUse an answer-retaining evaluator and link request IDs to scoresThe included probe does not preserve answer text or tool arguments for later scoring.
Benchmark scores used to choose a serving engine directlyMeasure quality first, then service performance for the qualified configurationPublisher scores do not measure the local engine, export, hardware or load.

These are methodological corrections and proposed engineering choices. They do not assert that an unexecuted configuration works.

A small benchmark menu with a purpose

Choose the relevant rows, plus held-out examples from the actual application. Do not run every public suite merely to produce a large table. Here, “held out” means withheld from local tuning; it does not establish that the examples were absent from model training.

DecisionProposed quality evidenceWhat to record and what it cannot establish
Does an engine/export preserve instruction following?IFEval, using the official strict and loose evaluation definitions; add application-specific formatting and multilingual casesReport prompt-level and instruction-level scores separately. Preserve raw responses and the extraction rule for the answer channel. This tests constrained instructions, not general factual accuracy. MB-IFEVAL
Does coding quality survive precision or speculation changes?A frozen LiveCodeBench code-generation release/date range; use EvalPlus HumanEval+/MBPP+ as a smaller regression screenFix problem IDs, tests, language/runtime, attempts and sampling. Report pass@1 under the declared attempt policy; multi-attempt pass@k requires its own sample design. Execute generated programs in the chosen isolated evaluator. Neither suite is a repository-agent benchmark, and a newer problem date alone does not prove no training overlap. MB-LIVECODEBENCH, MB-EVALPLUS
Is a larger context actually useful, and does cache reuse preserve it?RULER tasks plus held-out document questions with evidence references and answerable/unanswerable casesFreeze generated examples and seeds; report each task and length bucket. Vary evidence position and distractors in the application set. Synthetic retrieval success does not establish document reasoning, citation accuracy or a usable million-token service. MB-RULER
Do tools work across multiple turns?Relevant BFCL categories plus deterministic local tool fixturesRecord category/version, handler/parser and tools. Separate valid JSON, correct tool choice/arguments and final task success. A parser smoke test is not a BFCL score. Online search and other changing services require frozen fixtures or a clearly separate live-system evaluation. Fixture substitutions produce a local variant, not an official live-search score. MB-BFCL
Does the vision path retain useful quality?MMMU with a declared split and official scorer, plus application images/documents and matched text controlsPin image bytes, order, processor, resizing/cropping and answer extraction. Report text and image results separately. Visual-token capacity or a valid image request does not establish visual reasoning or OCR quality. Apply only after the exact checkpoint and endpoint qualify. MB-MMMU
Does an agent solve repository tasks?Optional SWE-bench evaluation with a named subset and a fixed agent scaffoldRecord agent/prompt/tool versions, environment images, task IDs, model-call/token/time budgets, retries and patch/test results. Use a unique evaluator run/cache namespace for every candidate and independent attempt; verify that saved reports correspond to the current patch and task manifest. Reused report paths can return stale scores. MB-SWEBENCH-EVAL The score belongs to the entire system. Report GPU inference separately from tool/test wall time. This is a later campaign, after the endpoint and simpler coding tests qualify. MB-SWEBENCH

Benchmark sources above define their tasks and evaluators. Their selection for this atlas is a proposed use, not evidence that they already provide a working adapter for every listed model. Check the pinned harness's endpoint, template and reasoning/tool handling before interpreting a score. If an adapter is missing, record the block and the required adapter validation; do not substitute an unlabelled prompt format.

Fresh source checks exposed evaluation defaults that need an explicit override or record:

  • RULER: the main README marks its old script pipeline deprecated and points to rulerv1-ns and rulerv2-ns. Choose the intended task version, then pin that branch commit and its NeMo-Skills dependency; a pin of the main README alone does not pin the runnable evaluator. MB-RULER
  • LiveCodeBench: select a fixed release/date range and record the lite/full test policy. Defaults that track the latest release do not produce a frozen comparison. Verify the actual loaded item IDs and date range. At the inspected commit, the full (--not_fast) code-generation loader does not apply the requested release/date filters; full-mode experiments need a separately validated pinned loader/filter and item manifest. MB-LIVECODEBENCH-LOADER, MB-LIVECODEBENCH-ROUTER Fix evaluator CPU/memory limits and test timeouts too; evaluator overload must not be misdiagnosed as a model regression. MB-LIVECODEBENCH
  • BFCL: preserve the expected item manifest and report missing/unevaluated categories. Its partial-evaluation option can exclude missing results, so a displayed score needs coverage and failure counts. MB-BFCL
  • MMMU: the official README reports test-answer publication on February 12, 2026. Public labels do not establish a fresh or uncontaminated final test; retain application examples held out from local tuning. MB-MMMU

Model-by-model priority

Every row starts with exact-artifact loading, protocol checks and a small scored text set. Priorities below reflect architecture and unresolved serving questions, not measured model rankings. The linked validation plans cite the publisher evidence, identify starting profiles and describe the controls in detail.

Family and detailed planFirst useful quality campaignServing comparison to attachSpecific uncertainty to resolve
Qwen 3.8 27BInstruction following, coding and image tasks; long-context/state testsBF16 target-only reference, then exact FP8/NVFP4 exports; TP1 and equal-node replicationQuantization quality and recurrent-cache behavior must be checked independently.
Gemma 4 31B ITInstruction following, image reasoning and long-distance evidence useBF16/FP8/NVFP4 with matched processing, thinking mode and cache policyLocal/global attention and image handling need coverage; qualify the SGLang export probe first.
GLM 5.3 FlashMulti-turn tools, image inputs, long-context state correctness and codingTarget-only, then supported MTP; backend/KV pairs and state-pool comparisonsA paired backend/dtype change is not an isolated KV-precision test; P/D needs separate real-weight qualification.
GLM 5.3Coding and multi-turn tools with fixed reasoning budgetsFP8 versus each exact NVFP4 export, matched KV where possible; TP/replica and MTP controlsExporter differences, automatic KV selection and total-node capacity can confound the conclusion.
Qwen 3.8 Flash NextLong-context and multi-turn correctness, coding, image tasksQualify the documented SGLang TP1 probe and vLLM TP8 path, then an equal-budget comparisonPLE/ngram placement, mixed MTP tensors and state precision need explicit records.
Kimi K3Coding, long multi-turn/tool histories and image quality on a qualified pathExact native versus mixed NVFP4 qualification; engine-compatible target/drafter and natural DSparkBlocked generic paths remain blocked; draft compatibility and rollback correctness precede speed claims.
DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731Coding/tools and sparse/compressed long-context accuracyExact July-31 target-only baseline, documented four-GPU topology, then eight-GPU adaptations and DSparkA nearby model version's support or parameter headline cannot qualify this release.
Mistral Medium 3.5Coding/tools, image questions and long-context quality at each reasoning settingPublisher TP8 baseline, then TP2/4 and replicas with matched KVWeight fit alone does not prove lower-TP capacity; no audited NVFP4 artifact is supplied.

Design one comparison before scaling it

  1. State the decision. Example: decide whether one exact Qwen 27B NVFP4 export preserves the declared coding and image quality requirements while increasing node capacity. First compare it with the qualified BF16 reference under matched serving settings. A separate topology experiment can then spend the freed memory. Do not attribute both changes to weight precision.
  2. Freeze the evaluation contract. Record benchmark version, dataset revision/split, selected item IDs/hash, scorer commit, metric definition, prompt adapter, answer extractor, few-shot examples, system prompt and model-specific chat template. Record image processor and tool schemas where applicable. Keep reference answers out of generation inputs. Use a development set to choose settings and a held-out set for the final decision. Keep the final set out of local quantization calibration, prompt/backend/precision selection and tuning. If an export does not disclose its calibration data, record that overlap is unknown; identify public-set training contamination uncertainty separately.
  3. Define budgets and failure policy. Pin all effective sampling settings, including temperature/top-p and any top-k/min-p/penalties or generation-config defaults, plus attempts, reasoning effort, output cap, stop strings, timeouts, retries and agent/tool budgets. Same effort labels across models need not mean equal computation. Compare both a declared budget policy and observed useful-answer quality, generated tokens and wall time. Keep reasoning and final-answer latency separate where the endpoint exposes them. Retain observed reasoning/final/total token counts when available; do not infer hidden counts from a single combined usage field.
  4. Check context before each request. Serialized text, tool schema, retained history and image tokens plus reserved generation must fit both model and launch limits. Record the actual token counts and truncation policy. A context-limit rejection is a recorded infeasible point, not permission to silently shorten a benchmark or discard it.
  5. Run paired quality and service campaigns. Use the same item IDs and frozen payloads for within-model A/B tests. Establish low-load quality, then score a preselected subset under realistic load, cache hits/eviction and cancellations. Replay cancelled sessions from the prescribed conversation state and score subsequent responses. Use enough independent repeats for the chosen uncertainty analysis; a screening subset is not a full benchmark score.
  6. Explain acceptance. Predeclare absolute task requirements and allowed degradation per critical stratum. For quality differences, estimate paired uncertainty at the independent item/session level, retaining correlations between multiple turns or attempts. A failed significance test is not evidence of equivalence. For a higher-is-better score, one proposed rule is Δ = candidate − reference: require the chosen lower confidence bound to be at least −allowed regression, and require the absolute task threshold to pass under its predeclared uncertainty rule. A confidence interval crossing the allowed regression boundary is inconclusive; one wholly below it fails the regression requirement. Reverse the direction for lower-is-better metrics. Freeze tuning budget and candidate count to limit selection bias; confirm the selected candidate on held-out work.

For within-model engine comparisons, require the same effective tokenization and template where supported. If endpoint serialization differs, investigate and either correct it or report a complete-serving-stack comparison. For cross-model comparisons, use identical task content and scorer with each model's valid template/tokenizer. Report their actual token counts; equal token counts across different tokenizers are not necessarily equal work. Rank useful task completion per elapsed time and resource budget, with the quality/latency constraints stated. Keep pure token-throughput charts within an explicitly comparable tokenization scope.

Separate completion, correctness and goodput

OutcomeRequired evidenceInterpretation
Protocol completedValid response framing and recognized finish reasonThe request reached a protocol endpoint, not necessarily a useful answer.
Task succeededSaved response plus a fixed scorer, tests or reviewed rubricThe answer met the task's definition; valid tool JSON alone is insufficient.
Latency objective metRequest timing with the declared start/end and budgetA fast refusal or truncated answer can satisfy timing while failing the task.
Quality-adjusted request goodputJoin all three outcomes for the same request ID; count qualifying requests over full measurement wall timeUnscored responses do not qualify. Report offered, completed, scored, failed, filtered, truncated and retried counts.
Latency-SLO goodput for a quality-qualified configurationA separate quality campaign passes; the load run measures successful requests within latency budgetsThis does not show that every timed answer was correct. Do not multiply throughput by an unrelated average benchmark score and call it measured quality-adjusted goodput.

For multi-turn tools or agents, score the complete task/episode. Count unique successful episodes and include every model call, tool step and retry in elapsed time and resource accounting. Request throughput is a separate diagnostic; it is not completed-task throughput.

The local streaming probe accepts length and content_filter as recognized protocol endings. Its ok and successful_requests_per_second are transport-level observations. It does not save answer text, reasoning or assembled tool calls; it cannot provide a quality artifact or score outputs after the run. It sends a fixed JSONL list and does not execute tool results or run an agent loop. Add an external answer-retaining evaluator for quality, and an open-loop client for controlled arrival-rate experiments. No such evaluator or adapter is implemented by this documentation update.

A length finish is a censored generation; report it even if a task scorer accepts the partial answer. Keep task success and truncation as separate fields and predeclare whether truncation disqualifies service acceptance. A refusal/filter response needs the task's policy-aware label. Retries consume time, tokens and requests: report first-attempt and retry-assisted success separately. Count resource consumption from failed attempts as well.

Minimum artifacts and decisions

Extend each experiment record with a quality suite manifest. For multiple suites, keep one manifest per suite and reference them through quality_evaluation.additional_suite_manifests. Each manifest must bind the selected items, payloads, raw answers and scores using stable item/request/attempt IDs. Preserve model and engine identities, effective settings, usage, finish reasons, timing, tool traces where applicable, and scorer errors. The template is manual: repository validation checks JSON syntax, not whether these fields are complete or scientifically sound.

When using a model judge, pin its identity, prompt, rubric and parsing, and audit a sample with human labels. Report disagreement and judge failures. Prefer executable tests or deterministic checks when they represent the task. Neither a judge score nor a benchmark aggregate proves that arbitrary application answers are factual.

Publish a decision table for each family: exact baseline/candidate, relevant task scores and paired uncertainty, failure/truncation counts, observed reasoning/output budget, whole-node goodput definition, tail latency, peak memory, and promote / reject / inconclusive / blocked with a reason. Start with a small fixed qualification campaign, expand only passing candidates, and retain the baseline for rollback. The next operator work is to select the application workload, thresholds, pinned evaluator/adapters and actual B300 environment; those inputs cannot be inferred from publisher cards.

companies/alibaba-qwen/README.md

companies/alibaba-qwen/qwen3.8-27b/architecture.md

Qwen 3.8 27B: architecture

Data flow

Vision/text → [GDN → GDN → GDN → gated full attention] × 16, with dense MLPs → output head; optional MTP.

How the parts work together

Three Gated DeltaNet layers are followed by a gated full-attention layer, repeated through the text backbone. The linear-attention path maintains a recurrent matrix state with a short convolutional component. Full-attention layers retain ordinary token-history cache. Consequently, the model has both a context-dependent cache and a concurrency-dependent state pool.

The key and value head counts in the linear path differ. The full-attention path has its own query-head count, KV-head count and head dimension. Deriving head dimensions by dividing hidden width by a familiar head count would produce the wrong shapes here; use the explicit configuration.

The feed-forward network is dense, not MoE. Every token traverses those linears; there is no expert-parallel switch that turns it into a sparsely activated 27B model. The vision encoder is shared infrastructure for image/video inputs, with spatial merging and temporal patching before language processing.

MTP is an optional additional serving path. It changes scheduling and temporary-state needs, not the base model’s dense-versus-MoE identity. The official context extension beyond the native window is not evidence that every engine, quantization and workload preserves useful accuracy at that length.

The architecture facts above are drawn from the publisher card and configuration; the workload consequences are analytical interpretation. qwen3.8-27b-CARD qwen3.8-27b-CFG

This is a selected, normalized projection, not a byte-for-byte copy of the complete config. Field labels have been made comparable across models. Layer counts are derived from text_config.layer_types; rotary_dim is head_dim × partial_rotary_factor; nextn_layers corresponds to text_config.mtp_num_hidden_layers. The extended-context claim comes from the card rather than the config.

Memory and performance consequences

A TP1 process is a memory-planning candidate on a 288 GB GPU. Multiplying the publisher's rounded 27B language-model headline by two bytes gives approximately 54 GB (50.3 GiB) at BF16. This is not a checkpoint byte census or a strict lower bound; vision, auxiliary modules and runtime allocations need separate accounting. Compare independent replicas with sharded layouts for total node goodput at the same workload and latency target.

For the 16 full-attention layers, conventional unpadded BF16 KV payload is 2 × 16 × 4 × 256 × 262144 × 2 bytes, or 16 GiB per native-length sequence. The recurrent matrix alone is 48 × 48 × 128 × 128 × 4 bytes, or 144 MiB per state slot at FP32. Convolution state, cached snapshots, speculative verification and allocator overhead are additional. Neither calculation measures an engine's complete state pool.

The numeric examples are calculations from stated dimensions and assumptions, not measured allocations. Memory mathematics explains the formulas and their limits. qwen3.8-27b-CARD qwen3.8-27b-CFG HW

What this report does not establish

Actual TP1 NVFP4 kernel efficiency on this B300 firmware/container combination; optimal hybrid-cache split; useful quality at the extended context; performance under the user’s language and tool distributions.

The public artifacts do not disclose every training-data, optimization or implementation detail. This report does not fill missing details with assumptions or present a complete formal reconstruction of private training.

Interpretation

Keep the BF16, official FP8 and NVIDIA mixed export as separate comparisons. The official FP8 config declares dynamic activations and 128×128 weight blocks; its exclusion list includes the vision tower, language head and selected recurrent components. The NVIDIA map assigns NVFP4 to 193 MLP/head module entries and FP8 to 208 attention projection entries, and excludes mtp*. These are metadata entries, not a tensor-byte census. qwen3.8-27b-FP8-CFG qwen3.8-27b-NV-CFG

Producer-version conflict: NVIDIA's card names ModelOpt 0.48.0 and local-Hessian calibration, but both pinned config.json and hf_quant_config.json record producer version 0.47.0.dev80+g913f5e224. The audit cannot reconcile the exporter version from these artifacts; preserve both observations when reproducing the checkpoint. qwen3.8-27b-NV-QUANT

The rounded weight arithmetic makes one B300 a plausible starting point; startup fit at the requested workload remains untested. NVFP4 may reduce bandwidth or permit more cache capacity, but quantization and kernel-launch overhead can offset that gain at low batch sizes. Benchmark the actual workload and retain BF16 as the quality reference.

qwen3.8-27b-CARD qwen3.8-27b-NV qwen3.8-27b-FP8 qwen3.8-27b-VR

Deployment rule

Pin the model revision, tokenizer/processor revision, quantization configuration, runtime commit and image digest together. A root BF16 dtype can coexist with quantized weights. The real contract includes serialized tensor types, scales, grouping, excluded modules, activation precision and runtime repacking. Do not cast a quantized checkpoint to BF16 and call it the original BF16 reference.

For every candidate, compare target-only quality against the appropriate reference before enabling lower-precision KV or speculation. Precision primer distinguishes NVFP4, MXFP4, FP8 and BF16. NV4 TE

companies/alibaba-qwen/qwen3.8-27b/serving.md

Qwen 3.8 27B: serving on 8×B300

Status: unbenchmarked local candidates. Publisher and engine recipes document support; this audit did not run an engine or benchmark the node.

Engine and topology

Begin with vLLM TP1 BF16 at 32K context, then the same FP8 and NVFP4 workload. Repeat with SGLang TP1. Keep vision enabled for multimodal validation and explicitly constrain its allowed input sizes; a text-only optimization must be a separate profile.

The supplied TP1 settings are controlled local experiments. NVIDIA's card documents a TP4 vLLM example and a SGLang example for its exact export; the current SGLang cookbook also lists that export. The cookbook pins FP8 KV, whereas the supplied SGLang comparison profiles pin BF16 KV. Record this difference and resolve vLLM's auto cache dtype before comparing results. The vLLM recipe's low-latency NVFP4 example uses an Inferact artifact, so its measurements do not establish NVIDIA-export performance.

Compare per-GPU replicas with TP2 and TP4 only after measuring single-request latency. The NVIDIA card’s TP4 long-context example is not evidence that TP4 maximizes node throughput for ordinary chat. For hybrid prefix caching, verify the recurrent-state path, not just token KV hits.

Use the correct thinking mode and sampling settings in benchmarks. Qwen’s documented thinking and non-thinking modes do not have identical generation defaults, so matching only temperature can still leave an unfair comparison.

Base, official FP8 and NVIDIA metadata revisions are pinned in sources and model.json. Pin the tokenizer/processor and actual runtime image as well. A revision identifies source artifacts; it does not validate installed kernels, multimodal execution or MTP behavior.

qwen3.8-27b-VR qwen3.8-27b-GR qwen3.8-27b-CARD qwen3.8-27b-NV HW

Experiment sequence

Measure TP1/2/4 with 1/8/32/128 concurrent requests; BF16/FP8/mixed NVFP4; 4K/32K/128K contexts; text-only versus image inputs; MTP off versus supported depths. Keep request payloads and thinking effort frozen.

First capture actual GPU memory, compute capability, peer topology and software versions with python scripts/preflight.py. Then resolve immutable model metadata, inspect the rendered profile and run the target-only correctness suite. Profiles live in profiles.

Acceptance gates

A successful load is necessary but insufficient. Require valid streaming framing, finite outputs, correctly separated reasoning, valid tool calls where supported, repeatable quality tests, bounded memory at load, and correct cache/state behavior after cancellation. Only then compare latency and throughput.

For production, place one sharded model process group inside a pod that owns its whole GPU group. Do not make eight independent KServe replicas and expect them to form TP8. Start with colocated prefill and decode; adopt disaggregation only after it wins the workload comparison and state transfer is correct. KS KSLLM

Parameters are not magic constants

The profile’s context cap is an application policy. Tensor parallelism is a starting layout. Memory utilization reserves room for non-weight allocations; changing it can trade cache space against startup headroom. Batch-token and sequence caps trade prefill efficiency against memory and queueing. Speculative depth trades draft/verification cost against naturally accepted tokens. Each must be varied one at a time before interaction testing.

Remaining uncertainty

Actual TP1 NVFP4 kernel efficiency on this B300 firmware/container combination; optimal hybrid-cache split; useful quality at the extended context; performance under the user’s language and tool distributions.

Decision and applicability

Proposed experiments; no GPU results. The question is which exact export and serving configuration gives useful capacity for a hybrid dense, multimodal service while preserving its quality. This model's 48 recurrent-attention layers and 16 full-attention layers make state handling a separate qualification from ordinary KV-cache reuse. The current cards/configs of all three artifacts matched their atlas pins when retrieved again on 2026-10-15 UTC. qwen3.8-27b-CFG, precision and provenance.

Start with the vLLM BF16 TP1 profile and SGLang BF16 TP1 profile. Qualify each pinned build before comparing engines. Resolve vLLM's auto KV dtype and match it to the other arm; the supplied SGLang profiles use BF16 KV, while upstream examples use FP8 KV. Weight format, KV dtype and recurrent-state dtype are three distinct controls. The NVIDIA export has mixed NVFP4/FP8 modules and an unresolved exporter-version discrepancy; neither a generic NVFP4 label nor an Inferact recipe qualifies these exact files. qwen3.8-27b-NV-CFG, serving.

The profiles cap context at 32,768 and active requests at 32. Begin with serialized inputs near 4K and 16K and output budgets of 128/1,024; include all template, reasoning-history and visual tokens in the length check. A 32K input plus output does not fit this cap. Longer input buckets and 128 active requests need separately qualified capacity settings. Native 262,144-token capacity and the publisher's 1M extension are subsequent experiments, with explicit positional overrides, memory and accuracy gates. Parser-free baseline profiles also need a pinned, qualified tool/reasoning configuration before they can evaluate those API features. qwen3.8-27b-CARD.

Architecture and export experiments

Q27-01 — Lower weight precision helps at a useful batch size.Within each qualified engine, compare pinned BF16, official block FP8 and NVIDIA mixed NVFP4 at TP1, first concurrency 1 and 8, then 32 if feasible. Keep effective KV/state precision, payloads and cache state fixed. Inspect exclusions and selected kernels at load.Save module/backend diagnostics, load/steady-state/peak memory, quality deltas and latency/goodput by workload. An unexpected fallback or quality failure disqualifies that arm. Distinguish reduced resident weights from increased cache reservation; a smaller file is not a measured speedup.
Q27-02 — Prefix reuse preserves both recurrent and full-attention state.Replay identical histories cold, warm and after eviction; add divergent suffixes around the build's cache/chunk boundaries. Interleave unrelated sessions, cancel during prefill and decode, then repeat. Sweep sequence length at fixed active count, then active count at fixed length; vary the supported state/KV pool split only after measuring demand.Record recurrent/convolution state slots, snapshots, KV occupancy, evictions, prefill reuse and allocation failures. Score planted answers against fresh-session controls. Stale cross-session content, lost suffixes or unrecovered pool allocation reject the candidate. Speed gains without correct state restoration do not pass.
Q27-03 — Thinking controls improve complete task outcomes.Freeze thinking mode, all sampling fields, reasoning effort and preserve_thinking for each engine/export A/B. Separately compare supported effort levels or preservation policies on the same multi-turn tasks, recording the resulting serialized histories.Report final-answer quality, first-answer latency, reasoning/final tokens, task completion time and retries. A preservation change changes the input and belongs to a separate service-policy comparison. Faster first reasoning output alone does not select a winner.
Q27-04 — Multimodal processing remains correct after export changes.Use the same image bytes, ordering, crop/resize policy and processor revision across exports. Add bounded videos only after the exact endpoint qualifies; freeze decoded frame identities, timestamps and sampling policy. Vary resolution or frame count in separate runs.Save visual-token counts, preprocessing/encoder time where exposed, TTFT, peak memory and image/video quality. Repeat text-identical requests with different images to detect cache-key mistakes. Frame-sequence input and a native video endpoint are different measurements; unsupported video is an applicability block.
Q27-05 — MTP repays draft, verification and rollback costs.After Q27-01/02, compare the SGLang target-only NVFP4 profile with its MTP candidate in the same build. Verify that the exact checkpoint's MTP tensors load. Start with the documented settings, then change only supported depth settings. Repeat at low load and near saturation.Retain natural accepted-length distributions with their denominator, draft/verification time, memory, rejection/rollback failures and quality. Include long coding, short chat and image-conditioned generation because acceptance can differ. Reject synthetic acceptance. MTP surviving a short chat does not establish hybrid-state correctness.
Q27-06 — Replication outperforms sharding for the intended traffic.For the best qualified export compare eight TP1 replicas, four TP2 groups and two TP4 groups, using all eight GPUs and the same offered arrival trace. Count router/CPU resources and preserve session/cache-routing policy. Fix total-node admission/concurrency and log per-group batching/scheduler limits before separate capacity tuning.Compare whole-node goodput, per-request tails, memory headroom and recovery after cancelling a busy request. Changed admission or batching policies require a complete-configuration comparison. Keep a separate single-group latency result; it cannot select node capacity. Dense MLPs provide no expert-parallel experiment.

The thinking/image/video interfaces and MTP recipes are publisher/engine documentation; the experiment designs and selection criteria above are local proposals. A supported payload format does not establish benchmark validity or quality. qwen3.8-27b-CARD, qwen3.8-27b-GR.

Quality tasks chosen for this model

Use the same frozen examples across BF16/FP8/NVFP4 and engine arms. A small preregistered subset can screen failures; promotion requires the declared full evaluation or an explicitly bounded application claim. Keep tuning examples separate from the final quality set. Publisher scores motivate coverage; they supply neither the expected local score nor a production threshold.

Task and primary sourceWhy it belongs here / controls and outputs
IFBench — MBENCH-IFBENCHVerifiable constraints exercise instruction following across quantization and thinking changes. Pin test data/verifiers and report prompt-level strict/loose results with failure categories. Score the final answer after the validated parser. The maintainer's temperature-zero evaluation is a distinct policy from Qwen's recommended sampled serving settings; label both if used.
LiveCodeBench — MBENCH-LCBExecutable code-generation tasks are useful for long decode and MTP acceptance. Freeze release_v6 or an explicitly chosen newer date window, data revision, sample count, prompt adapter and evaluator limits; report pass@1 and truncations. release_latest is unsuitable for repeated A/B runs. A local score does not reproduce the card's v6 score without matching its harness.
RULER v1 — MBENCH-RULER-V1Retrieval, tracing and aggregation at increasing lengths can reveal state/precision regressions that a single needle misses. Freeze the RULER and linked NeMo-Skills commits, tokenizer, generated examples and task mix. Report task-by-length scores and failures. Modified cache-boundary cases are labelled local regressions, outside the standard aggregate.
MMMU-Pro — MBENCH-MMMUPROImage-dependent reasoning checks the complete multimodal path. Choose standard(10 options) or vision and report them separately; pin prompt mode and preserve each image-placeholder mapping. Record per-subject accuracy and image tokens. A text-only score cannot qualify a mixed export for images.
BFCL — MBENCH-BFCLAfter parser qualification, use declared offline function-selection/argument and multi-turn categories. Report semantic call correctness separately from JSON validity. Pin the handler and tool environment; a category subset is not the overall leaderboard score.
Held-out application images and videosAdd document questions and temporal-order/counting questions with known answers and a written rubric. Include changed-image and reordered-frame controls. Report video completion and answer accuracy separately from single-image results; an image benchmark does not establish temporal understanding.

Run record and promotion

Use the shared model benchmark guide, protocol and a filled experiment manifest. Predeclare quality floors and permitted regressions per relevant task, latency/error budgets, useful goodput improvement, memory reserve and uncertainty method. Unknown thresholds block promotion. Randomize A/B order, repeat independently, retain failed requests and report uncertainty on paired quality and service differences. If the improvement interval crosses the declared useful threshold, the decision is inconclusive.

Deliver raw outputs/scores, request records, effective dtype/kernel/state-pool logs, processor/template hashes, startup and cancellation evidence, plus a decision for each workload and mode. The result schema describes the HTTP/SSE probe only; it does not score code, tools, images, videos or quality, and does not turn SSE chunks into exact token timings. Empty results mean not measured.

companies/alibaba-qwen/qwen3.8-flash-next/architecture.md

Qwen 3.8 Flash Next: architecture

Data flow

Text/image/video inputs → vision processing where needed + token embeddings → 12 groups of three GDN/MoE layers and one QSA/MoE layer → output. Gated residual branches span the backbone; n-gram/PLE features enter at its second layer. MTP adds an optional serving path.

How the parts work together

The backbone combines three recurrent Gated DeltaNet layers with a sparse-attention layer in each four-layer group. Qwen describes a selection budget of 512 four-token micro-blocks, or 2,048 tokens. That budget limits selected attention history; it is not the model's context limit or a complete cache-size formula. The output remains autoregressive.

A large n-gram embedding table provides an additional lookup path for local token patterns. It changes the balance between arithmetic and table access. The PLE configuration identifies where that representation is injected; treating it as an ordinary vocabulary embedding or dropping it because it is not in the 125B headline would change the model.

The main MoE selects ten routed experts plus one shared expert. Alongside it, the publisher describes four residual branches with data-dependent read gates and per-branch write gates. The configuration field hc_count alone does not establish equivalence to another model family's hyper-connection mechanism.

When MTP is enabled, its loader must respect its own expert precision, which differs from the main routed experts in NVIDIA's export. A target-only load cannot establish that this speculative path works.

The architecture facts above are drawn from the publisher card and configuration; the workload consequences are analytical interpretation. qwen3.8-flash-next-CARD qwen3.8-flash-next-CFG

Configuration extraction

This is a selected, normalized projection, not a byte-for-byte copy of the complete config. Counts are derived from text_config.layer_types; its twelve full_attention labels implement QSA according to the publisher card. rotary_dim is head_dim × partial_rotary_factor, and the two linear head dimensions both equal 128. The shared-expert count and extended-context claim come from the card. ple_layer_ids: [2] denotes the second backbone layer; the NVIDIA quantization map names its zero-based tensor path layers.1.ple. qwen3.8-flash-next-NV-CFG

Memory and performance consequences

The publisher's rounded language-model accounting is 125B main + 51B n-gram + 4B MTP, approximately 180B in that scope. This sum is not an exact tensor census and does not separately account for the vision encoder. The 6B activated headline applies to the main path; it should not be divided by this combined scope to claim a precisely defined sparsity ratio.

NVIDIA's quantization metadata marks the n-gram embedding as FP8. Applying one byte to the rounded 51B headline gives approximately 51 GB (47.5 GiB), before scales, padding and placement effects. The main experts' four-bit arithmetic does not cover this component. Measure table placement, lookup locality, transfer bandwidth and tail latency when comparing host offload with GPU residency. qwen3.8-flash-next-NV-QUANT

The numeric examples are calculations from stated dimensions and assumptions, not measured allocations. Memory mathematics explains the formulas and their limits. qwen3.8-flash-next-CARD qwen3.8-flash-next-CFG HW

What this report does not establish

B300 load, quality and performance for the documented SGLang NVIDIA TP1 recipe; n-gram placement costs; full checkpoint tensor-byte census; production throughput under realistic prefix reuse.

The public artifacts do not disclose every training-data, optimization or implementation detail. This report does not fill missing details with assumptions or present a complete formal reconstruction of private training.

Qwen 3.8 Flash Next: precision and provenance

VariantExact artifactActual precision contractEvidence
bf16Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-NextBF16 declared by text configPublisher card and pinned config inspected

Interpretation

The official FP8 config declares dynamic activations and 128×128 weight blocks, excludes attention/shared-expert modules, and explicitly includes the PLE n-gram embedding. The card and config were directly inspected at revision 236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13. qwen3.8-flash-next-FP8-CFG

NVIDIA describes W4A4 NVFP4 for the main routed experts, BF16 attention/shared components, 128×128 block FP8 for MTP routed experts, and per-tensor FP8 for the PLE embedding. The pinned maps confirm 48 NVFP4 expert-module entries, one FP8 PLE entry and one block-FP8 MTP entry. They use different MTP algorithm labels: FP8_PB_WO in config.json and FP8_BLOCK_SCALES in hf_quant_config.json. Record both files rather than replacing them with a single inferred format label. qwen3.8-flash-next-NV-CFG qwen3.8-flash-next-NV-QUANT

The card names vLLM commit d4d703caf908786416585ceb1f369e2e0363358b for target-only support and PR #55513 for MTP. GitHub confirms that PR merged on September 8, 2026 as 60ad959b6f1a5c8f602edbd608c8decbc0788c50. The installed image must contain the relevant changes. NVIDIA's TP8 MTP example enables expert parallelism: the 640-wide expert intermediate dimension divided by eight would be 80, which does not satisfy a 128-wide block boundary. This explains the documented constraint; it is not a local load test.

qwen3.8-flash-next-CARD qwen3.8-flash-next-NV qwen3.8-flash-next-VR QPR

Deployment rule

Pin the model revision, tokenizer/processor revision, quantization configuration, runtime commit and image digest together. A root BF16 dtype can coexist with quantized weights. The real contract includes serialized tensor types, scales, grouping, excluded modules, activation precision and runtime repacking. Do not cast a quantized checkpoint to BF16 and call it the original BF16 reference.

For every candidate, compare target-only quality against the appropriate reference before enabling lower-precision KV or speculation. Precision primer distinguishes NVFP4, MXFP4, FP8 and BF16. NV4 TE

License provenance

Qwen Community License 1.0; NVIDIA derivative also names NVIDIA Open Model License. This is a provenance flag, not legal clearance. The ZIP contains no model weights. Original model terms and derivative exporter terms remain separate from this repository’s original code and prose.

companies/alibaba-qwen/qwen3.8-flash-next/serving.md

Qwen 3.8 Flash Next: serving on 8×B300

Status: unbenchmarked local candidates. Publisher and engine recipes document support; this audit did not run an engine or benchmark the node.

Engine and topology

The supplied vLLM target-only candidate uses the exact NVIDIA export at TP8 and 65,536 tokens. The separate TP8 MTP candidate adds expert parallelism and one speculative token, following NVIDIA's layout while using a lower context cap. The supplied SGLang profile adapts its documented B300 TP1 target-only cell, with local caps of 65,536 tokens, 32 requests and a 0.82 static-memory fraction.

SGLang PR #41046 added exact NVIDIA-export recipes for B200/B300/GB300 and names version 0.5.20 or later. Its immutable generator selects TP1, FlashInfer linear-attention prefill/decode and BF16 recurrent state; it explicitly marks these cells verified: false. This supplies a concrete compatibility candidate, not B300 measurements. The profile retains that boundary. qwen3.8-flash-next-GPR qwen3.8-flash-next-GR-SOURCE

The base, official FP8 and NVIDIA metadata revisions are recorded in sources and model.json. NVIDIA's card supplies the exact NVFP4 TP8/MTP example; the current vLLM recipe's principal TP4+EP example uses the official FP8 export. Keep their checkpoint identities, KV settings and speculative depths distinct. Pin the actual runtime image before execution.

qwen3.8-flash-next-VR qwen3.8-flash-next-CARD qwen3.8-flash-next-NV HW

Experiment sequence

Compare SGLang TP1 target-only with vLLM TP8 target-only, accounting for total GPUs consumed and effective cache/state dtypes. Then evaluate TP4 capacity experiments, TP8+EP with one-token MTP, and alternative proposal depths after accuracy checks. Track n-gram placement, lookup stalls, recurrent-state allocation, indexer time and total node goodput.

Use the pinned publisher card and tokenizer template for thinking controls and sampling. The current SGLang cookbook's claim that this model always thinks conflicts with the publisher card, which documents enable_thinking and separate thinking/non-thinking sampling settings. Treat that cookbook prose as stale. qwen3.8-flash-next-GR

First capture actual GPU memory, compute capability, peer topology and software versions with python scripts/preflight.py. Then resolve immutable model metadata, inspect the rendered profile and run the target-only correctness suite. Profiles live in profiles.

Acceptance gates

A successful load is necessary but insufficient. Require valid streaming framing, finite outputs, correctly separated reasoning, valid tool calls where supported, repeatable quality tests, bounded memory at load, and correct cache/state behavior after cancellation. Only then compare latency and throughput.

For production, place one sharded model process group inside a pod that owns its whole GPU group. Do not make eight independent KServe replicas and expect them to form TP8. Start with colocated prefill and decode; adopt disaggregation only after it wins the workload comparison and state transfer is correct. KS KSLLM

Parameters are not magic constants

The profile’s context cap is an application policy. Tensor parallelism is a starting layout. Memory utilization reserves room for non-weight allocations; changing it can trade cache space against startup headroom. Batch-token and sequence caps trade prefill efficiency against memory and queueing. Speculative depth trades draft/verification cost against naturally accepted tokens. Each must be varied one at a time before interaction testing.

Remaining uncertainty

B300 load, quality and performance for the documented SGLang NVIDIA TP1 recipe; n-gram placement costs; full checkpoint tensor-byte census; production throughput under realistic prefix reuse.

Decision and prerequisites

Proposed campaign; no GPU results. Determine whether the NVIDIA mixed export can deliver useful whole-node capacity while preserving sparse retrieval, recurrent state, n-gram lookups and multimodal quality. Its 125B main-model headline omits the separately reported 51B n-gram table and 4B MTP component. The 36 GDN layers and 12 QSA layers need separate state/history accounting; a 2,048-token sparse selection budget is not a cache or context cap. Architecture, qwen3.8-flash-next-CARD.

Planning evidence was refreshed on 2026-10-15 UTC (October 16 in Paris). Current publisher card/config bytes match the pinned base revision; the current base, official FP8 and NVIDIA repository revisions match model.json. Use those identities in a separate experiment manifest for every arm. A recipe or successful target-only load does not certify all mixed tensors, MTP or B300 performance.

Starting arm or featureApplicability gate
vLLM NVIDIA TP8Qualify target-only loading of ModelOpt main experts, FP8 PLE and all excluded modules; record effective sparse-cache and recurrent-state dtypes and actual table placement. Pin reviewed remote code along with the image.
SGLang NVIDIA TP1The upstream source cell says verified: false. First prove loading, quality and memory headroom at the intended workload. Its BF16 state override differs from the base config's FP32 declaration; record the runtime dtype in both engines before comparing them. qwen3.8-flash-next-GR-SOURCE, qwen3.8-flash-next-CFG.
Official FP8 or BF16 quality referenceSeparate load/topology qualification; neither has a supplied profile for this family. The FP8 export's 128-wide blocks constrain expert sharding, so do not copy the NVIDIA target-only TP8 layout blindly. Use a supported common TP/EP layout when comparing exports. qwen3.8-flash-next-VR.
vLLM NVIDIA MTPRequires the mixed FP8 MTP path in the actual image. The profile adds EP and disables FlashInfer autotuning as well as enabling MTP. Its target-only control must use those same settings. With plain TP8, 640/8 = 80 does not meet the MTP expert block width of 128. qwen3.8-flash-next-NV.

Inspect both NVIDIA quantization maps: their MTP labels differ (FP8_PB_WO versus FP8_BLOCK_SCALES). Preserve this distinction and verify the loader's resolved tensor/group treatment; do not infer a uniform four-bit checkpoint. An exact index/header census of stored tensor bytes and per-rank runtime measurements remain prerequisites for memory claims. qwen3.8-flash-next-NV-CFG, qwen3.8-flash-next-NV-QUANT.

Quality workloads and why they belong

Apply the shared benchmark selection and evaluation rules, including frozen evaluation contracts, paired uncertainty and an answer-retaining scorer. Use its EvalPlus functional screen and a frozen LiveCodeBench release/date range before an expensive repository-agent campaign. Report pass@1, invalid programs and evaluator failures under the same language/runtime, attempt policy and budgets for each export and thinking mode.

WorkloadProposed evaluation and rationaleEvidence boundary
QSA/GDN long historyPin RULER v1 and its NeMo-Skills dependency; use fixed retrieval, variable-tracking and aggregation payloads at increasing lengths. Place required evidence at different positions and add held-out application questions spanning several documents.Score each task/length. Synthetic retrieval does not prove reasoning over real documents or the advertised extended context. Pin the current v1 pipeline rather than the deprecated main-branch runner. MBENCH-RULER-V1, MBENCH-RULER.
Instructions and tool argumentsRun pinned IFEval with prompt-level strict accuracy; add English/Chinese structured requests, identifiers, escaped strings, multi-turn tool results and known expected arguments. These test export quality and errors that table-heavy or multilingual traffic may expose.Keep validity and semantic correctness separate. Public-benchmark results complement a held-out application set and do not establish a causal n-gram effect. MBENCH-IFEVAL.
Image understandingUse a fixed single-document DocVQA validation set with official ANLS scoring, plus distinct local multi-image/follow-up regressions. Freeze images, processor, resize settings and answer extraction.Report quality, visual-token counts, encoder/preprocessor time and wrong-image answers. Single-image accuracy does not qualify video; a video campaign must freeze sampled frames/timestamps and labels separately. MBENCH-DOCVQA, MBENCH-DOCVQA-EVAL.
Coding deployment, if requiredUse SWE-bench Verified with a pinned agent harness, task images, tool rules and token/turn/time budgets, followed by an untouched evaluation set after tuning.Report resolved tasks and full task wall time, including tool latency. This is independent application evaluation, not reproduction of the NVIDIA or Qwen coding scores. MBENCH-SWEBENCH.

Keep thinking and non-thinking as separate workload strata. The publisher documents enable_thinking, preserve_thinking, reasoning_effort and different sampling settings for the two modes; the SGLang cookbook's contrary prose is stale. Save the serialized conversation so preserved reasoning changes cannot masquerade as cache or engine gains. Measure first final answer as well as first reasoning content. qwen3.8-flash-next-CARD.

NVIDIA's paired FP8/NVFP4 table is exporter evidence, not a local quality gate. Its declared max_new_tokens=131072 and reasoning_effort=xhigh do not fit the current 65,536-token profile as a reproduction setup. Retain its numbers as attributed results; any attempted reproduction needs the original evaluation protocol, adequate context/output budgets and a separately qualified capacity configuration. qwen3.8-flash-next-NV.

Ordered experiments

IDControlled comparison and mechanismMeasurements and decision
QFN-01: mixed loadQualify each stored target-only profile on stable and one pinned candidate build. Audit stored main/PLE/MTP/vision components separately from resident target tensors and documented loader exclusions; record serialized bytes versus host/HBM residency, repacking and transient peaks.A TP1 recipe passes only if all required target components, including PLE and the enabled vision path, plus the desired working set fit with the declared reserve. Deliberate target-only MTP omission is valid and must be inventoried. Reject missing required tensors, unplanned dtype expansion or unexplained fallback; qualify MTP residency in QFN-05.
QFN-02: export qualityOn a qualified common engine/build and TP/EP layout, compare official FP8 with NVIDIA NVFP4, keeping sparse KV, GDN state, table placement, sampling and processor fixed. Add BF16 only after separate qualification.Produce paired quality deltas and task failures, plus actual load/steady-state memory. If no common supported layout/dtype exists, report a complete configuration comparison and do not attribute the result to weight precision alone.
QFN-03: n-gram placementOnly where the exact export/backend supports it, compare GPU-resident PLE with the documented host-offload path. Hold table contents/precision, NUMA placement, CPU allocation and all serving controls fixed. Replay both repeated local-token-pattern and diverse identifier/multilingual cohorts with cold prefix caches.Measure actual table/scale bytes, host pinned memory, transfer bandwidth, lookup stalls and p95/p99 latency under concurrency. Keep each cohort identical across arms. A synthetic locality win does not predict real traffic; removing PLE would change the model.
QFN-04: GDN/QSA stateCompare identical logical requests from fresh prefill, warm prefixes, divergent suffixes, eviction and cancellation, interleaving unrelated sessions. Shift evidence across four-token QSA micro-block neighborhoods and actual backend chunk/cache boundaries; include histories exceeding the selection budget.Report retrieval/task scores by length/position, state and sparse-cache pools, reuse counters and continuation errors. Preserve recurrent/convolution state as well as selected token history. Qualify any supported BF16/FP32 state change as its own quality experiment.
QFN-05: mixed MTPFirst create a qualified TP8+EP, autotuning-disabled, speculation-off control matching the MTP profile. Qualify the speculative arm's MTP tensors/scales and FP8 precision, then compare its one-token MTP arm; deeper proposals follow shape and quality checks.Confirm FP8 MTP execution, record natural acceptance, verification/draft work, state rollback, stop handling and memory. Measure both low load and sustained traffic. The stored plain-TP8 target-only arm does not isolate MTP because it also differs in EP and autotuning.
QFN-06: whole nodeAfter individual qualification, compare one vLLM TP8 group with a measured, disjoint SGLang TP1 replica count up to the eight-GPU budget. TP4/EP or other replica layouts require new manifests and load gates. Match offered traffic and include routing/cache locality.Report consumed GPUs, whole-node goodput, first-answer tails, CPU/storage pressure and memory per replica. Do not multiply a TP1 result by eight or call TP1 versus TP8 an equal-resource engine result. Use the same tuning budget and report remaining dtype/layout differences.

The inspected vLLM target loader explicitly filters mtp. weights. Its target-only resident inventory can therefore be smaller than the stored checkpoint without losing a required target component. Check the chosen image's registered path and account for added MTP memory when enabling speculation. MBENCH-QFN-TARGET-LOADER.

Use complete serialized input buckets of 4,096, 16,384, 32,768 and 61,440 tokens with 128/1,024 output caps, plus a 4,096-input/8,192-output generation trace. Count image/template/reasoning tokens within the current 65,536 cap and report achieved lengths and truncations. Begin at concurrency 1 and 8, then 32 and a fixed offered-rate ladder; include short chat mixed with long document/image prefill. Separate cold and repeated-prefix runs. Quality evaluations receive a budget sufficient for final answers rather than inheriting short shape-probe caps.

Extension toward native 262,144 context and any YaRN path toward 1M are separate experiments. Pin the positional-scaling configuration, retest short as well as long prompts, and establish load/state capacity before evaluating accuracy. An extended-context publisher claim is not a result for these profiles.

Required outputs and promotion

Deliver a complete manifest, quantization/tensor-placement audit, raw request and response records, quality scores by mode/task/modality/length, table/state/KV memory, profiler evidence for lookup or communication claims, and a paired decision table. Follow the protocol for repeated randomized comparisons, uncertainty, offered load and failures. The client result schema does not replace quality or tensor-placement evidence.

Declare quality/regression thresholds, latency/error budgets, memory reserve and minimum useful improvement before running. Reject missing required target or enabled-draft tensors, corrupted continuation, failed quality gates or inability to sustain the stated workload. A faster result with inadequate uncertainty or missing effective dtype/placement evidence is inconclusive. Preserve failed and unmeasured arms explicitly; no B300 winner or production SLA is implied.

companies/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731/architecture.md

DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731: architecture

Data flow

Tokens → recent-window + compressed selected history → mHC streams → hash/routed experts → output; bundled DSpark features → proposals → target verifies.

How the parts work together

The configuration exposes several interacting mechanisms: compressed attention representations, indexed sparse retrieval, a short sliding window, multiple hyper-connected streams, and routed experts. Its compression schedule alternates different compression ratios after the initial uncompressed layers. Draft-related entries also appear in the serialized schedule, so its length must not be used as the main layer count.

The local window protects access to recent tokens while the compressed and selected representations provide longer-range access. A sparse index budget is a selection budget, not the model’s maximum context length. The maximum positional setting and the available GPU cache are again separate constraints.

The model uses a specific router score function and scaling, plus bounded SwiGLU behavior. A generic MoE wrapper that changes the gate normalization or clipping would alter inference even if every checkpoint tensor loaded successfully.

The release bundles DSpark-related structure, including selected target-layer features and a Markov component. The configured block size, an engine’s proposal count, and the number of tokens emitted after verification are different quantities. Never “correct” the checkpoint’s block setting to match an example CLI argument without checking that implementation’s semantics.

The architecture facts above are drawn from the publisher card and configuration; the workload consequences are analytical interpretation. deepseek-v4-flash-0731-CARD deepseek-v4-flash-0731-CFG

This is a selected, normalized projection, not a byte-for-byte copy of the complete config. Field labels have been made comparable across models. Layer indices explicitly state zero-based or one-based conventions.

The full 46-entry compression array is retained in model.json. The root config's num_nextn_predict_layers=1 is metadata, not a verified count of DSpark stages: the same revision's reference inference config sets n_mtp_layers=3, and its implementation builds three DSparkBlock stages under mtp.*. That namespace does not make the checkpoint compatible with an ordinary MTP speculative method. The reference loop also confirms that target feature IDs 40, 41 and 42 are zero-based. Reference inference config, reference implementation.

Memory and performance consequences

Do not read quant_method=fp8 as an all-FP8 model: the same configuration explicitly sets expert_dtype=fp4. Likewise, a single generic GQA formula does not represent all compressed caches, indexes, windows and draft state in this architecture.

The vLLM recipe uses the preview-family headline 284B total / 13B active, while the SGLang cookbook labels the exact 0731 variant 304B / 13B. These differently scoped figures are not a verified main-plus-draft tensor census. The catalog keeps exact total and active counts unset until that accounting is reconciled; Hugging Face serialized-element totals also include packing and auxiliary tensors. vLLM recipe, SGLang cookbook.

A 1,048,576-token positional ceiling follows the configured YaRN factor 16 and original 65,536 positions; that equality does not measure usable cache or long-context quality. Memory mathematics explains the formulas and their limits. deepseek-v4-flash-0731-CARD deepseek-v4-flash-0731-CFG HW

What this report does not establish

Exact main-plus-draft parameter accounting; selected image and kernel provenance; local B300 capacity, throughput and application correctness; qualification of the local eight-GPU adaptations.

The public artifacts do not disclose every training-data, optimization or implementation detail. This report does not fill missing details with assumptions or present a complete formal reconstruction of private training.

DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731: precision and provenance

Reverified 2026-10-15 (UTC) at 7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062. No checkpoint was loaded locally.

VariantExact artifactPrecision evidence
nativedeepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731Root config sets expert_dtype=fp4 and separately declares FP8 e4m3 with ue8m0 scales and 128×128 weight blocks

Interpretation

The official artifact is mixed precision. Its reference loader packs two FP4 expert values per byte and uses one E8M0 scale per 32 expert values. The 128×128 blocks in the root quantization config describe the FP8 path, not those FP4 expert groups. Other tensors can retain higher precision. This is not an all-FP8 checkpoint, and four-bit expert storage alone does not identify an NVFP4 export. Root config, reference implementation.

The vLLM recipe's optional FP4 indexer cache changes a separate attention-cache representation. Keep it off during the initial correctness comparison, then measure retrieval quality and performance when enabling it. The checkpoint's FP4 expert weights do not mandate that cache setting. vLLM recipe.

Engine execution precision can differ from serialized precision. Select the intended expert backend and inspect its actual load/repacking path before comparing memory or speed. SGLang documents flashinfer_mxfp4 for the exact 0731 FP4 route; the atlas's vLLM candidate follows the documented deep_gemm_mega_moe route. These names are not evidence that both execute the same weight and activation arithmetic. Publisher serving examples.

Deployment rule

Pin the model and tokenizer revisions, quantization configuration, runtime commit and image digest together. Root BF16 metadata can coexist with quantized weights. Inspect serialized tensors, scales, excluded modules, activation precision and runtime repacking. Casting a quantized checkpoint to BF16 does not reconstruct an original BF16 reference.

Compare target-only quality before changing cache precision or enabling DSpark. The precision primer explains the formats, and the serving report keeps publisher recipes separate from local experiments.

License provenance

The pinned LICENSE file is MIT. The same revision's model card explicitly applies that license to the repository and model weights. This verifies the named artifact's stated terms; it does not establish terms for separately named derivatives. No model weights are bundled here. LICENSE, model card.

companies/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731/serving.md

DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731: serving on 8×B300

Status: unbenchmarked local recommendations. The upstream recipes are evidence of documented support, not a benchmark of your node.

Engine and topology

Use the documented vLLM TP1/DP4 plus expert-parallel layout as the initial four-GPU baseline. The DP8/EP profile is an explicit eight-GPU adaptation. Expert parallelism reuses the data-parallel group; it is not another factor multiplying the GPU count. Both local profiles impose a 64K cap, FP8 KV and the DeepGEMM MegaMoE backend. The chosen image still needs to pass correctness checks for this exact revision. vLLM recipe.

The publisher also documents the exact 0731 checkpoint with SGLang TP4, flashinfer_mxfp4 and bundled DSpark. SGLang's cookbook reports an end-to-end run of that command on 4×GB300 with v0.5.16. This is upstream evidence, not a local eight-B300 result. The included SGLang TP8 target-only profile remains a compatibility probe because it changes that topology and omits speculation. Publisher card, SGLang cookbook.

Preserve the producer's encoding contract: this release supplies Python message-encoding/parsing helpers instead of a Jinja chat template. Check reasoning fields, tool boundaries and streaming. The engine parser names differ: vLLM documents deepseek_v4; SGLang documents reasoning parser deepseek-v4 and tool parser deepseekv4. A fluent answer alone does not verify that protocol. Encoding documentation, vLLM recipe, SGLang cookbook.

DSpark weights are bundled with the target. SGLang instructs users to omit a separate draft-model path; its documented default proposes five tokens and verifies six. The vLLM recipe uses seven proposals. These engine choices do not rewrite the checkpoint's dspark_block_size=5. Match sampling too: the publisher's vLLM example uses greedy drafting, while the current recipe selects probabilistic drafting. Treat each as a distinct experiment and keep the client sampling fixed. Publisher card, vLLM recipe, SGLang cookbook.

The 64K local cap is deliberately restrictive. DeepSeek recommends allowing up to 384K output tokens for high/max effort; those requests cannot fit this cap. Compare engines under the same shorter application budget, or create a separately qualified long-output profile. Publisher usage guidance.

Experiment sequence

Compare target-only with native DSpark, natural acceptance, and identical prompts. Test 4-GPU versus 8-GPU EP layouts, index-cache precision and 16K/64K/128K prompts. Validate tool calls, reasoning boundaries, EOS handling and the first token after a cancelled speculative request.

First capture actual GPU memory, compute capability, peer topology and software versions with python scripts/preflight.py. Then verify local metadata against the immutable revision in model.json, inspect the rendered profile and run the target-only correctness suite. Profiles live in profiles.

Acceptance gates

A successful load is necessary but insufficient. Require valid streaming framing, finite outputs, correctly separated reasoning, valid tool calls where supported, repeatable quality tests, bounded memory at load, and correct cache/state behavior after cancellation. Only then compare latency and throughput.

For production, place one sharded model process group inside a pod that owns its whole GPU group. Independent KServe replicas do not assemble a distributed TP/DP/EP engine group. Start with colocated prefill and decode; adopt disaggregation only after it wins the workload comparison and state transfer is correct. KS KSLLM

Parameters are not magic constants

The profile’s context cap is an application policy. Tensor parallelism is a starting layout. Memory utilization reserves room for non-weight allocations; changing it can trade cache space against startup headroom. Batch-token and sequence caps trade prefill efficiency against memory and queueing. Speculative depth trades draft/verification cost against naturally accepted tokens. Each must be varied one at a time before interaction testing.

Remaining uncertainty

Exact main-plus-draft parameter accounting; selected image and kernel provenance; local B300 capacity, throughput and application correctness; qualification of the local eight-GPU adaptations.

All GPU and quality experiments below are proposed, not measured. The metadata audit was performed on 2026-10-15 (UTC). For this plan, current and pinned publisher cards/configs were retrieved again at 2026-10-15 22:51 UTC and still match base revision 7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062 in model.json. Engine recipes were freshly read as dated documentation, not as local runtime results.

What needs a decision

Determine whether the exact July-31 release serves the application's coding, tool and long-document work correctly, and whether a larger GPU group, a smaller indexer cache or DSpark improves useful capacity. The earlier sweep did not specify encoding checks, a long-context scorer or an equal-node comparison. This plan makes those controls explicit. Use the shared benchmark selection guide, protocol and experiment record for the common evaluation contract and decision rules.

Keep weight, MLA cache, indexer-cache and C4/C128 compressed-attention-state precision separate in the manifest. The root num_nextn_predict_layers=1 is not a reason to truncate the three reference DSpark stages. Configuration, reference inference configuration, precision explanation, SGLang cookbook.

Before any of those scores, run encoding round trips for plain chat, thinking and multi-turn tools. Compare the actual serialized token sequence with the pinned helper for the same messages. Cover string versus JSON-valued tool arguments, parallel call/result ordering, streamed delimiter fragments, EOS and stop handling.
